notFound.text: This page does not exist, or you do not have access to it.

validation.projectKey: 2–10 characters: a letter first, then letters, digits or _

setup.title: Welcome to BuggyWuggy
setup.intro: Create the first administrator account to get started.
setup.tokenHelp: Printed in the server log at startup (or set with BUGGYWUGGY_SETUP_TOKEN).
setup.done: The administrator has been created. You can log in now.

login.title: Log in
login.codeIntro: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
login.codeHelp: Lost your phone? Enter one of your recovery codes instead.
login.recoveryCodeUsed: You logged in with a recovery code; {{count}} unused codes left.
login.recoveryCodesLow: Ask an administrator to reset your two-factor login to get new recovery codes.

sso.failed: Logging in with single sign-on did not work. Try again, or ask your administrator.
sso.cancelled: The login at the identity provider was cancelled.
sso.unknown-provider: This single sign-on provider is not configured.
sso.unavailable: The identity provider cannot be reached at the moment. Try again in a minute.
sso.no-account: You have no BuggyWuggy account yet. Ask your administrator to create one.
sso.inactive: Your BuggyWuggy account has been deactivated.
sso.email-not-verified: Your e-mail address is not verified at the identity provider, so it cannot be linked to your BuggyWuggy account.
sso.already-linked: This BuggyWuggy account is already linked to another identity at this provider. Ask your administrator.
sso.username-taken: An account with your username already exists. Ask your administrator to link it.
sso.email-taken: An account with your e-mail address already exists. Ask your administrator to link it.
sso.invalid-username: Your username at the identity provider cannot be used in BuggyWuggy. Ask your administrator.
sso.no-email: The identity provider gave no e-mail address. Ask your administrator.

projects.title: Projects
projects.keyHelp: Used in issue keys, e.g. KEY-123.

project.name: Name
project.notFound: This project does not exist, or you do not have access to it.
project.noIssues: This project has no issues yet.

issue.deleteConfirm: The issue and its history are deleted permanently.
issue.deleteConfirmWithSubtasks_one: The issue, its sub-task and their history are deleted permanently.
issue.deleteConfirmWithSubtasks_other: The issue, its {{count}} sub-tasks and their history are deleted permanently.
issue.deleteConfirmEpic_one: The epic is deleted permanently. The issue in it is kept, but no longer belongs to an epic.
issue.deleteConfirmEpic_other: The epic is deleted permanently. The {{count}} issues in it are kept, but no longer belong to an epic.
issue.notFound: This issue does not exist, or you do not have access to it.
issue.conflict: This issue was changed in the meantime. The latest version is shown now; please try again.
issue.labelsHelp: Press Enter, space or comma after each label.

comment.title: Comments
comment.conflict: This comment was changed in the meantime. The latest version is shown now.

attachment.title: Attachments
attachment.drop: Drop files here to attach them.
attachment.tooLarge: {{name}} is too large. Files can be at most {{max}}.
attachment.tooLargeTotal: These files are too large together. One upload can be at most {{max}}.

link.title: Linked issues
link.otherIssuePlaceholder: Type a key or words to search

taskwarrior.showCalculation: Show how the urgency was calculated
taskwarrior.resolved: Resolved issues have no urgency, as TaskWarrior's next report only lists pending tasks.
taskwarrior.noTerms: Nothing about this issue counts towards its urgency.
taskwarrior.explanation: Each line: the issue's value for a term × the term's coefficient = its share. The coefficients are set by the administrator in the configuration file.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.intro: Global permissions apply to all of BuggyWuggy, not to one project. They are granted to groups. Members of a group that gains or loses a permission are logged out and get the change at their next login — that includes you, if you are a member.

help.ADMINISTER: Manage users, groups and global permissions; archive, delete and re-key projects; change the settings of every project.
help.CREATE_PROJECT: Create new projects. The creator becomes the project lead and administrator.
help.BROWSE_USERS: Find users and groups by name, e.g. to filter issues or to fill project roles.

user.search: Search by name, username or e-mail
user.systemAdminHelp: Has every permission everywhere, and can manage other system administrators.
user.createHelp: New users are added to the users group.
user.activeHelp: Inactive users cannot log in, but their name stays on their issues and comments.
user.passwordSet: The password of {{name}} has been set.
user.setPasswordHelp: The user is logged out everywhere and must log in with the new password.
user.groupsHelp: When membership of a group with global permissions changes, the user is logged out and gets the new permissions at the next login.
user.twoFactorEnrolled: Set up: the user logs in with a code from an authenticator app.
user.twoFactorNotEnrolled: Not set up. When two-factor login is switched on, the user sets it up at the next login.
user.resetTwoFactorText: Use this when {{name}} lost the phone with the authenticator app, or the recovery codes. The secret and the recovery codes are removed, {{name}} is logged out everywhere, and sets up two-factor login again at the next login.
user.twoFactorReset: The two-factor login of {{name}} has been reset.
user.ssoOnlyHelp: No password: the user logs in through the identity provider. The account is linked at the first login.
user.ssoNone: Not linked to an identity provider yet.
user.ssoHelp: After unlinking, the next login through the provider is a first login again: it is linked or refused as the provider's settings say.

group.name: Name
group.builtInHelp: Built-in groups cannot be renamed or deleted.
group.deleteConfirm: Delete the group {{name}}? Its members are kept, but lose the permissions and roles the group gave them.

mail.testSent: A test mail has been sent to your e-mail address.
mail.notConfiguredHelp: Set buggywuggy.mail.host and the other mail settings in {{file}} and restart BuggyWuggy. See the Installation Guide.
mail.notConfiguredNoFile: BuggyWuggy runs without a configuration file. Create one (for example /etc/buggywuggy/application.yml) with buggywuggy.mail.host and the other mail settings, and restart BuggyWuggy with --spring.config.additional-location=file:/etc/buggywuggy/application.yml. See the Installation Guide.
mail.queueCounts: {{pending}} waiting · {{sent}} sent in the last 24 h · {{failed}} failed
mail.templatesIntro: Each mail has a template per language. Users get mails in the language of their profile, or in the default language. Choose a language to edit a template.
mail.customizedLegend: ✎ = changed by an administrator. The other templates are the built-in ones.
mail.languagesIntro: Mails can be sent in the enabled languages. A language without own templates uses those of the default language.
mail.languageCodeHelp: A code such as de or pt-br
mail.deleteLanguageConfirm: Delete the language {{name}} and its templates? Users who chose it get mails in the default language.
mail.failedIntro: These mails could not be sent, even after several attempts. Check the mail settings and try again.
mail.subject: Subject
mail.builtInHelp: This is the built-in template. Saving makes it your own version.
mail.bodyHelp: Keywords between double braces are replaced when the mail is sent.
mail.resetConfirm: Replace this template by the built-in one? Your version is lost.
mail.resetDone: The built-in template is used again.

importer.intro: Copy the issues of another issue tracker into BuggyWuggy, with their comments, attachments and history. Original authors and dates are kept; nobody is notified by e-mail.

forgejo.name: Forgejo
forgejo.description: Issues of a repository on a Forgejo server, such as codeberg.org or your own installation.
forgejo.title: Import from Forgejo
forgejo.urlHelp: The address you open Forgejo at, e.g. https://codeberg.org.
forgejo.tokenHelp: Optional; needed for private repositories. Create one in Forgejo under Settings → Applications, with read access to repositories, issues and users. An administrator token also shows e-mail addresses, so more people are matched to existing accounts. The token is only kept in memory while BuggyWuggy runs, never stored.
forgejo.connectedAnonymous: Forgejo {{version}}, without a token: only public repositories.
forgejo.searchHelp: Part of the name, or owner/repository. Empty with a token: your own repositories.

jira.name: Atlassian Jira
jira.description: Jira Cloud, or Jira Server / Data Center at your own address.
jira.title: Import from Jira
jira.urlHelp: The address of your Jira: https://your-site.atlassian.net for Jira Cloud, or that of your own Jira Server or Data Center (with its path, e.g. https://example.org/jira).
jira.userHelp: Jira Cloud: your e-mail address. Jira Server / Data Center: your username, or leave it empty when you use a personal access token.
jira.tokenHelp: Jira Cloud: an API token (Account settings → Security → API tokens). Server / Data Center: a personal access token (Profile → Personal Access Tokens), or your password. Leave both empty for a public Jira. It only needs to read; the importer never changes anything in Jira. The token is only kept in memory while BuggyWuggy runs, never stored.
jira.connectedAnonymous: {{version}}, without logging in: only public projects.
jira.searchHelp: A project key (ABC) or part of the name. Empty: all projects you can see.

gitlab.name: GitLab
gitlab.description: Issues of a project on gitlab.com or a self-managed GitLab.
gitlab.title: Import from GitLab
gitlab.urlHelp: https://gitlab.com, or the address of your own GitLab (with its path, if it has one).
gitlab.tokenHelp: Optional for public projects; needed for private ones and for e-mail addresses. Create a personal (or project or group) access token with the read_api scope under Preferences → Access tokens. It only needs to read; the importer never changes anything in GitLab. The token is only kept in memory while BuggyWuggy runs, never stored.
gitlab.connectedAnonymous: GitLab, without a token: only public projects.
gitlab.searchHelp: Part of the name, or the full path (group/subgroup/project). Empty with a token: your own projects.

github.name: GitHub
github.description: Issues of a repository on github.com or GitHub Enterprise Server.
github.title: Import from GitHub
github.urlHelp: https://github.com, or the address of your GitHub Enterprise Server.
github.tokenHelp: Required: without a token GitHub allows only 60 requests an hour. Create a fine-grained personal access token under Settings → Developer settings, with read-only access to the repository's issues and metadata (or a classic token with the repo scope for private repositories). It only needs to read; the importer never changes anything on GitHub. The token is only kept in memory while BuggyWuggy runs, never stored.
github.searchHelp: Part of the name, or owner/repository. Empty: your own repositories.

redmine.name: Redmine
redmine.description: Issues of a project in a Redmine installation.
redmine.title: Import from Redmine
redmine.urlHelp: The address of your Redmine, with its path if it has one (e.g. https://example.org/redmine).
redmine.userHelp: Only to log in with your username and password; leave it empty when you use an API key.
redmine.tokenHelp: Your API key (My account → API access key), or your password. Either only works when the administrator turned on the REST web service (Administration → Settings → API). Leave both empty for public projects. It only needs to read; the importer never changes anything in Redmine. The key is only kept in memory while BuggyWuggy runs, never stored.
redmine.connectedAnonymous: {{version}}, without logging in: only public projects.
redmine.searchHelp: A project identifier or part of the name. Empty: all projects you can see.

trac.name: Trac
trac.title: Import from Trac
trac.urlHelp: The address of the Trac environment, e.g. https://trac.example.org/project. Trac must have the TracXMLRPC plugin.
trac.userHelp: Your Trac username. Leave it and the password empty to read as anonymous (who then needs the XML_RPC permission).
trac.tokenHelp: Your password. The user needs the XML_RPC and TICKET_VIEW permissions; the importer only calls methods that read, and never changes anything in Trac. The password is only kept in memory while BuggyWuggy runs, never stored.
trac.searchHelp: A Trac environment is one project; it is listed below.

job.title: Import of {{source}}
job.retryHelp: Runs the import again with the same settings; only what is new is imported. You are asked for the access token again if it was used.
job.retryHelpToken: Runs the import again with the same settings and the token still in memory; only what is new is imported.
job.tokenAgain: The access token is no longer in memory. Enter it again, or leave it empty for a public repository. For Jira with an e-mail address or username: enter it as e-mail:token.
job.logHelp: The log is also written to the application log of BuggyWuggy (e.g. journalctl).

wizard.numbering: Imported issues get new numbers in the project, in the order of their original numbers. The original number and a link to it are kept on the issue and in its history.
wizard.found: {{issues}} issues ({{open}} open, {{closed}} closed), {{comments}} comments, {{milestones}} milestones or versions. Pull and merge requests are not imported.
wizard.alreadyImported: {{count}} of these issues were imported before. They are not imported again; only their new comments are added.
wizard.issueTypeHelp: For issues without a label that sets the type.
wizard.labelsHelp: Keep a label as label (spaces become hyphens), use it to set the issue type or priority, turn it into a component, or leave it out. Issue types of the source are listed as type:Name; Jira's priorities and components as priority/Name and component/Name.
wizard.label: Label
wizard.usersHelp: People who reported or are assigned to issues. Choose the BuggyWuggy account for each, or leave it on automatic: first by e-mail address, then by username, otherwise a placeholder account is created (inactive, cannot log in). Commenters are matched automatically.
wizard.summary: {{issues}} issues of {{repository}} on {{url}} will be imported into {{project}}.
wizard.willNumber: Issues get new numbers; the original number is shown on the issue and in its history.
wizard.willHistory: Comments, attachments, watchers, milestones (as fix versions), dependencies, sub-issues and the original history are imported with their original authors and dates.
wizard.willPullRequests: Pull requests (merge requests in GitLab) that referenced an issue, and Jira's web links, are kept as links to the original.
wizard.willNotMail: Nobody gets e-mail about imported issues.
wizard.willNotStoreToken: The access token is not stored; you can retry an import without typing it again until BuggyWuggy restarts.
wizard.willSkip: {{count}} issues imported earlier are skipped; only their new comments are added.
wizard.willSubIssues: Sub-issues of a standard issue become its sub-tasks; deeper levels are linked with “relates to”.
wizard.willOnlyRead: The importer only reads: nothing is changed in the source.

settings.title: Project settings
settings.keyHelp: Changing the key changes all issue keys; the old keys keep working.
settings.keyAdminOnly: Only BuggyWuggy administrators can change the key.
settings.defaultAssigneeHelp: Who new issues are assigned to when nobody is chosen.
settings.archivedNotice: This project is archived: its issues can be viewed, but nothing can be changed. Ask a BuggyWuggy administrator to restore it.
settings.archivedNoticeAdmin: This project is archived: its issues can be viewed, but nothing can be changed. Restore it under Details to make changes.
settings.archiveHelp: Hides the project from the project list and makes it read-only. Can be undone.
settings.unarchiveHelp: Makes the project visible and editable again.
settings.deleteHelp: Deletes the project with all its issues, comments and attachments. Cannot be undone.
settings.deleteWarning: This permanently deletes the project with all its issues, comments, attachments and history.
settings.deleteTypeKey: Type the project key {{key}} to confirm
settings.componentsIntro: Components are parts of the product, for example "Backend" or "Documentation".

component.name: Name
component.deleteConfirm: Delete the component {{name}}? It is removed from all issues.
component.leadRequired: Choose a lead to assign issues to the component lead.

settings.versionsIntro: Versions are releases of the product. Their order here is the order in which they are offered.

version.name: Name
version.deleteConfirm: Delete the version {{name}}? It is removed from all issues.
version.datesInvalid: The release date cannot be before the start date.

settings.rolesIntro: Roles decide what people may do in this project: Users can see and create issues, Developers can work on them, Administrators can change these settings. Add groups or individual users to a role.

profile.title: Profile
profile.timeZoneHelp: Stored with your profile for later use. The web interface shows times in the time zone of your browser ({{zone}}).
profile.passwordHelp: You stay logged in here; your other sessions are logged out.
profile.languageHelp: Language of the e-mails you get. The web interface is in English for now.
profile.emailNotificationsHelp: About issues you watch, reported or are assigned to. Several changes by one person are combined into one mail.
profile.notifyOwnChangesHelp: Normally you do not get mails about changes you made yourself.
profile.ssoOnly: You log in with single sign-on, so you have no BuggyWuggy password.

board.title: Board
board.readOnly: You can look at this board, but not move issues on it.
board.unmapped: Issues with the status {{statuses}} are not shown: these statuses are in no column.
board.truncated: Only the first {{count}} issues are shown.

cannot.transition: You may not change the status of issues in this project.
cannot.assign: You may not assign issues in this project.
cannot.edit: You may not edit issues in this project.
cannot.rank: You may not change the order of the issues on this board.
cannot.noPriority: An issue cannot be moved to the lane without priority.
cannot.epic: Issues of type {{type}} cannot be moved to another epic on the board.
cannot.noTransition: There is no transition from {{status}} to a status in {{column}}.

config.defaultIntro: The columns of the board of every project that has no columns of its own. Each column shows the issues with one of its statuses; moving an issue to another column changes its status through the workflow. Project administrators can give their project columns of its own.
config.projectIntro: The columns of this project's board. Each column shows the issues with one of its statuses; moving an issue to another column changes its status through the workflow.
config.usesDefault: This project uses the default board, set by the BuggyWuggy administrator. Saving gives the project these columns as its own.
config.noStatuses: No statuses: the column stays empty
config.unused: In no column, so not shown on the board: {{statuses}}.
config.swimlanesHelp: The horizontal lanes until a user chooses others.
config.resolvedDaysHelp: How long resolved issues remain on the board.

donate.title: Support BuggyWuggy's continued development
donate.intro: BuggyWuggy is free and open-source software. Organisations can help sustain its development and maintenance through an optional annual contribution.
donate.freedom: BuggyWuggy is free software. Free as in freedom, not as in free of charge: you may use, study, change and share it under the GNU Affero General Public License. That freedom does not mean that making it costs nothing.
donate.people: Real people work on BuggyWuggy. They write and review the code, fix bugs, answer questions and keep it secure and up to date, often in their own time.
donate.continuity: Your donation keeps the project going and makes new features possible.
donate.loginAsAdmin: Log in as a BuggyWuggy administrator to view the suggested annual contribution for your organisation and request a quotation.
donate.comicAlt: xkcd 2347, Dependency: all modern digital infrastructure rests on a project some random person in Nebraska has been thanklessly maintaining since 2003.
donate.comicAttribution: <work>“Dependency” (xkcd 2347)</work> by Randall Munroe, licensed under <license>CC BY-NC 2.5</license>.

expired.title: Support expired
expired.text: Renew your annual contribution to continue supporting BuggyWuggy development.

license.why: Free software is about freedom, not price
license.whyText: Developing and supporting BuggyWuggy takes time. If your organisation uses it, please support the project with an annual donation: it keeps BuggyWuggy maintained, and the login page shows this installation as an active supporter while the donation code is valid.
license.validUntil: The donation code is valid until {{date}}.
license.attribution: Prices are based on the Big Mac index of The Economist (source data licensed under CC BY 4.0).

quotation.title: Request a quotation
quotation.intro: Choose your country and the number of users to see the suggested annual contribution. It follows the cost of living in your country, measured by the Big Mac index. Send the request, and you will hear from us with an invoice and a donation code.

quote.calculation: {{base}} per user per month in the Netherlands × the price of a Big Mac in {{country}} ({{bigMac}}) / in the Netherlands ({{reference}}), Big Mac index of {{date}}.
quote.noIndex: {{base}} per user per month: the Big Mac index has no price for this country.

sent.title: Quotation request sent
sent.text: Your request has been sent to {{to}}. You will receive a donation code for the challenge below.
sent.queued: The request waits until mail is configured (Administration → E-mail). You can also send it yourself to {{to}}:
sent.mailto: Open it in your mail program

activate.title: Enter the donation code
activate.intro: Enter the donation code you received for one of the challenges below. The login page then shows this installation as an active supporter until the donation code expires.

license.unlicensed: This BuggyWuggy installation does not support the project yet
license.unlicensedText: Free software is about freedom, not price: developing and supporting BuggyWuggy takes time. Please support the project with an annual donation.
license.expired: The support of this BuggyWuggy installation has expired
license.expiredText: Renew your annual contribution to continue supporting BuggyWuggy development.

twoFactor.title: Set up two-factor login
twoFactor.intro: This BuggyWuggy installation requires a code from an authenticator app at every login, besides your password.
twoFactor.scan: Open an authenticator app on your phone (for example Aegis, FreeOTP, Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator) and scan this QR code.
twoFactor.qrAlt: QR code with the two-factor secret
twoFactor.manual: Cannot scan? Enter this key in the app instead:
twoFactor.openApp: Open in the authenticator app on this device
twoFactor.verifyIntro: Enter the 6-digit code the app now shows for {{issuer}}, to check that it works.
twoFactor.recoveryIntro: Two-factor login is set up. Keep these recovery codes in a safe place, apart from your phone: each logs you in once when you do not have your phone. They are shown only now.
twoFactor.saved: I have saved my recovery codes

about.license: BuggyWuggy is free software under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 or later:
about.askAdmin: Your administrator can request a donation quotation under Administration → Donation.
